chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Billy Strayhorn: a real musician
summary: Brown calls Strayhorn underrated and cites Lush Life, Chelsea Bridge and I Want Something to Live For.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Thought I heard that. How about Billy Strayhorn?

Well I'm not sure whether I told you before, but to me Billy Strayhorn was one of the most underrated musicians that I've ever known. He was a real, real musician. A musician to me is a person who gets his material through the influence from say, you take a trip and you look at the mountains or you go across a certain bridge and you get the feeling of beauty and you interpret it and it's musically -- or those kind of things and they put them down in music. To me that is the real musician. That was the real Strayhorn. If you've ever heard the tune that he wrote called, 'Lush Life,' which is a tune that he brought into the organization in the late '30's, now he was writing, composing/playing that type of music and writing that type of music
way back then and until today no one has ever played "Lush-life" in the exact way that Strayhorn wanted it to be played.

He is really a terrific musician. Now, take another tune called, "Chelsea Bridge." And if you could stretch your imagination a little bit you can almost see Chelsea Bridge in his music same way as you can see the Grand Canyon Suite when you hear the Grand Canyon Suite. And most of his tunes -- what was another tune of his that was terrific? All of his tunes have a deep feeling behind them and one that I particularly liked was, "I Want Something to Live for."
See all of these he writes the music and the words and everything himself and you hear him in his music which is to me the mark of a real musician. See?
